title: An AAC-friendly outing note
summary: A short handoff can help staff, hosts or activity leaders understand how to communicate without turning a person’s private history into a public briefing.

title: Make the ordinary day a little easier.
summary: A place for the bag, a meal with fewer steps, a calendar people can actually use. Start with the small household difficulties that keep coming back.

title: The one-page caregiver handover
summary: A handover should make the next few hours clearer, not turn into a biography. Put the practical plan first and keep private care information in the secure places it belongs.

title: A family command center that earns its wall space
summary: The useful command center is not the one with the most features. It is the place everyone knows to check for today, tomorrow and the few things that are easy to forget.

title: A short plan you can actually use.
summary: Three fill-in tools for an ordinary week: a leaving-the-house card, a one-good-thing day plan and a household handoff. Fill them here, copy them or print a blank set.

title: Good clothes. Ordinary days. Plenty of repeats.
summary: A comfortable waistband, a useful layer, something ready for the pool. Build around the clothes people actually want to wear, with enough room for their own taste.

title: Frog Pond
summary: The whole Common can feel like a city day. Frog Pond can be just one thing: summer spray, winter skating, or the carousel. Pick the season, do the one thing, then find a bench.

title: Great Brook Farm
summary: It has the perfect simple-good-things formula: a working dairy farm, a short walk if you want it, and ice cream. The park is enormous; your visit does not need to be.

title: LaCascia’s
summary: It can be lunch, a familiar takeout stop, a pastry box, bread for home or the thing that prevents you from cooking. Useful food is a legitimate outing category.

title: Marginal Way
summary: The ocean is right there almost immediately. The mistake is deciding the only legitimate visit is the entire path from end to end. Pick an access point, walk until the view has done its job, sit, turn…

title: Battle Road
summary: You do not have to ‘do’ the whole Revolutionary War. Pick one trailhead, one piece of history, maybe one ranger program, and let the woods and old road do the rest.

title: New England Aquarium
summary: Water is inherently regulating for many people, but aquariums are also echoey, dim, crowded and full of transitions. The Aquarium earns a place here because it publishes concrete sensory supports…

title: Walden Pond
summary: The history is lovely. The water is the reason the outing works. On the right day, the best plan is beach, one short walk, look at the cabin replica, and leave before the parking lot becomes an ordeal.

title: Wegmans Burlington
summary: There are days when the best family logistics tool is a predictable slice of pizza plus tomorrow’s groceries in the same building. Favorite places do not all need hydrangeas.

title: Wildwood Park
summary: Playground, walking laps, a field, done. The ordinary park can be exactly the right answer when the transition cost of a ‘real outing’ is bigger than the outing itself.

title: The Book Barn
summary: A used bookstore that feels like its own little world: books outside, books inside, gardens, odd corners, animals, and permission to wander without a prescribed route.

title: Codman Community Farms
summary: Sometimes the best local outing is not an attraction. It is seeing the animals, walking a familiar path, buying something from the farm store, and going home.

title: deCordova Sculpture Park
summary: Art without needing everyone to stand quietly in a gallery. The sculpture park lets you move, look, sit, skip things and keep the visit yours.

title: Drumlin Farm Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: The gift of Drumlin is that it can be a real outing without becoming a project. Animals, trails, familiar geography, and home is still close.

title: Gilsland Farm Audubon Center
summary: A gentle nature stop just outside Portland with space, birds, meadow views and the kind of pacing that does not ask you to perform family fun.

title: Kittery Food Mart + Fort McClary
summary: One of our favorite Maine lunch plans: pick up inexpensive local food at Kittery Food Mart, then take it to Fort McClary and actually have lunch at the picnic area overlooking the water.

title: Life Time Burlington
summary: For us, water can be the whole plan. An indoor pool and whirlpool make this a dependable reset when weather, daylight or outdoor logistics are not cooperating.

title: L.L.Bean Flagship
summary: A store that can function like a destination: walk around, look at the trout pond, get a coffee, sit for a minute, buy nothing or buy the one thing you came for.

title: Misty Harbor Resort
summary: Not a precious hotel. A useful one: more room, an indoor pool, a hot tub, a short ride to the beach, and enough practical structure to make one night feel like a getaway.

title: Pineland Farms
summary: A choose-your-own-adventure place where the mistake would be trying to do all of it. Farm, gardens, market, trails: pick one.

title: Quiero Cafe
summary: A colorful Portland food stop where empanadas and other handheld options can make lunch feel fun without requiring a formal restaurant plan.

title: Rancatore’s Ice Cream
summary: Why Rancatore’s—Ranc’s—stays on our local favorites list: homemade ice cream, an easy tiny-outing formula, practical access notes and a printable Lexington field guide.

title: Rococo Ice Cream
summary: A genuinely special ice-cream stop that can still be just an ice-cream stop. Pick a flavor, enjoy the beautiful little moment, and keep the rest of the day loose.
location: Kennebunk, Maine · our Kennebunkport-area sweet stop

title: Scarborough State Beach
summary: A big Rhode Island beach where the accessibility information is unusually useful: pavilions, ramps and beach-mobility equipment give you concrete things to ask for instead of vague 'accessible' language.

title: Sherman’s Maine Coast Book Shop
summary: A bookstore is one of the best kinds of travel stop: climate-controlled, low commitment, interesting to different ages, and nobody needs to agree on the same thing to look at.

title: Watch Hill + Napatree Point
summary: This is the glamorous New England postcard — but the useful guide has to say the inconvenient part too: parking is the hard bit, and Napatree itself does not give you bathrooms or lifeguards.

title: Wells Beach
summary: A beach day does not need chairs, games, a cooler the size of a toddler and six hours of commitment. Wells is very good at the simple version.

title: Wilson Farm
summary: A grocery run that can feel like a small New England outing: produce, bakery, prepared food, seasonal displays and something good to bring home.

title: Wolfe’s Neck Center
summary: A coastal farm where the free version is already a real outing: animals, trails, open space and the feeling that you got out of the car somewhere distinctly Maine.

title: York + the Nubble
summary: The Nubble is one of those rare very-pretty things that does not require a hike or an admission ticket. You can make the whole visit ten minutes if that is the day you are having.

title: The familiar-food plan for days out
summary: The goal is not a perfect restaurant experience. It is knowing what food is available, what you can bring and what the backup is before hunger turns into the hardest part of the day.

title: A little thought before the ribbon.
summary: The best starting point is the person receiving it: what they enjoy, what they use and what will fit comfortably into their life. A gift should feel good to receive.

title: The hotel + pool checklist
summary: A suite, an indoor pool and a lovely photograph are not enough information. Confirm the room, the water, the timing and the complete price before the reservation becomes the plan.

title: Five, fifteen or thirty minutes to a more usable home.
summary: A room-by-room reset for the time and energy actually available. Start with the walking route, make one space useful and stop at a clear finish line.

title: Worth the space. Worth the effort.
summary: A good-looking product is a beginning. The useful questions come after that: what does it solve, what does it ask of you, and will anyone want to use it?

title: Three thoughtful gifts, made with what is already at home.
summary: Exact supplies, simple assembly steps and words for the tag. Make a tea-break packet, a pocket memory album or a useful list wallet without a last-minute shopping trip.

title: A cupboard meal that makes room for company.
summary: Keep one flexible four-person meal on the shelf: tomato-and-white-bean pasta, separate toppings and a fruit finish. Here are the quantities, timing, substitutions and food-safety checks.

title: Communication is an ecosystem, not a device.
summary: A practical, evidence-informed guide to multimodal communication: speech, AAC, gestures, signs, pictures, writing, eye gaze, switches, partner-assisted scanning, low-tech backups and emerging AI access.

title: One good plan. Room to enjoy it.
summary: The pretty part is easy to find. These are the details that help a family day out or a weekend away actually work: beds, food, water, waiting, and somewhere to pause.

title: Their interests. Their choices. The help they need.
summary: An older teen can need substantial support and still want a say in clothes, activities and everyday life. Begin with the person, then make the practical details work around them.

title: A better swim outing for an older teen
summary: The best swim plan is age-respectful, practical and built around the person who is actually getting in the water — not around what an activity is ‘supposed’ to look like.

title: The low-drama photo-day plan
summary: A good photograph does not require a brand-new personality, a complicated outfit or an hour of styling. Make the familiar version look a little more intentional and protect the routine around it.

title: Good photographs deserve a life off the phone.
summary: Make a small, personal gift from photographs you already own: a six-photo envelope, a folded memory card or a ready-to-frame print. Keep the people and the moment exactly as they were.

title: Pack once. Reset after the swim.
summary: A practical bag system for a pool visit or one-night trip, with a per-person packing list, a ten-minute departure check and a five-minute unpacking plan.

title: Make room for the whole person.
summary: High support needs are part of everyday family life here. So are preferences, humor, privacy, favorite places and the pleasure of a day that works.

title: Build a quiet-break plan before you need it
summary: A break works better when nobody has to invent it in the middle of a crowded place. Decide where, how and what comes next while everyone is still calm.

title: A New England rainy-day outing plan
summary: Rain does not have to cancel the day, but it does make transitions, wet clothes and backup food more important. Keep one main plan and one easy escape hatch.

title: The sensory-friendly clothing checklist
summary: Start with the clothes that already feel right, then shop the details: seams, waistbands, closures, fabric, care and whether the piece still feels age-appropriate.

title: The shorter-visit plan
summary: Decide the small version of the outing before you arrive. It makes leaving a valid part of the plan instead of something that feels like the day went wrong.

title: Things we have bought. Questions worth asking.
summary: A small, concrete starting point for the kitchen, gift drawer and household. These items have verified purchase records; the notes explain what to check before buying your own.

summary: A compact template for holding onto your priorities when the meeting begins to move quickly.
